entries.title: Uniform one-arm criterion for graph exhaustions (draft)
entries.statement: Draft analysis awaiting independent review: Let G be an infinite connected locally finite graph, o a vertex, and G_n increasing subgraphs containing o that exhaust its vertices and edges. At a fixed common Bernoulli bond parameter p define a_n(R)=P_p(o connects in G_n to ambient graph distance at least R). Finite path witnesses and continuity of probability give theta_G(p)=inf_R sup_n a_n(R), whereas theta_G_n(p)=inf_R a_n(R). Hence absence of an infinite origin cluster in G requires, and is equivalent to, a radius R for each epsilon>0 that bounds a_n(R) by epsilon simultaneously for every n. Separate radius limits for each n do not supply this quantifier order.
assumptions: Infinite connected locally finite ambient graph
Increasing vertex-and-edge exhaustion with common origin

entries.title: Independent cut bound for finite-width lattice strips (draft)
entries.statement: Draft calculation awaiting independent review: In independent nearest-neighbor bond percolation on S_k=Z x {-k,...,k}, with finite integer k>=0, p<1 and integer R>=1, the origin's probability of connecting to a vertex with |x|>=R is at most 2[1-(1-p)^(2k+1)]^R. Each interface between adjacent columns has 2k+1 edges; its all-closed event has probability (1-p)^(2k+1), and interfaces use disjoint bonds. Thus each fixed strip has p_c=1. The rate deteriorates with k, so this estimate does not establish absence of percolation in the increasing union.

entries.title: Nonpercolating strips with a percolating increasing union (draft)
entries.statement: Draft counterexample awaiting independent review: For the same parameter p=99/100 every finite-width strip S_k=Z x {-k,...,k} has no infinite Bernoulli bond cluster, while their increasing union Z^2 percolates. An enclosing closed dual circuit count gives theta_Z2(p)>=1-10557/2352250000>0.99999. Consequently unrestricted transfer of nonpercolation from every approximating graph to its union is false, even when every graph is infinite, connected, locally finite and quasi-transitive. This example is supercritical in the plane and the strip critical probabilities do not converge to the planar critical probability; it does not refute critical nonpercolation on higher-dimensional lattices or a bridge with additional threshold hypotheses.
assumptions: Finite widths before each radius limit

entries.title: Dated critical-percolation status and proof receipts
entries.statement: The intermediate-dimension critical bond-percolation target asks theta_d(p_c(d))=0 on nearest-neighbor Z^d for every integer 3<=d<=10. A September 2026 public preprint claims the broader quasi-transitive bond theorem. The current status is UNKNOWN in this analysis because the full recent proof has not been independently verified. A comparator theorem whose body is by sorry is an admitted statement, not a proof receipt; this alone does not refute a separate paper. A dated assertion of openness must retain its date until a current source and proof are checked.
assumptions: Current status verification requires the actual proof and assumptions

relations.rationale: The counterexample uses the independent-cut estimate to establish nonpercolation in every fixed approximating strip.
The exact exhaustion identities explain the two distinct orders of radius and width limits in this counterexample.
A proposed exhaustion route to the exact critical target must justify its width/radius quantifier exchange. This criterion supplies no critical uniform bound and does not solve the target.
